instruction:
Read docs/TASK_PHASE17.md FIRST (all of sections 1-4, 6 and 7), then in contour.yaml group dashboard-ui: Wire Page (description, behavior with its paragraph "Phase 17 (layout)", examples 1-9) and Style Page (description, behavior, examples 1-8), the Requirement Frontend Tree and the Guardrail Frontend Isolation. Every id, class, data attribute, text and colour value you need is there; do not invent names.

You own three files. (1) dashboard/src/main.ts: the phase-16 file is in your context; keep its polling, timers, error handling and exports exactly as they are (examples 1-5 still hold) and add the phase-17 layout: `import "./style.css";`, the sections with titles and captions, the select inside #events with [data-field="feed-meta"], the static .feed-head and ul.legend, class "dash" on #app, and doc.title. Use statusOf and formatTime from ./format; no logic of your own beyond wiring. (2) dashboard/src/style.css, new: the whole look, plain CSS, styling the elements main.ts and the four renderers make (the renderers are in your context and must not change: read their element types and data attributes). Use the custom properties of Style Page with exactly its values. Aim for a page an analyst leaves on a second monitor all night: calm and dense, the status pill and block number readable from across the room, the event feed the largest panel, everything else quiet context; small uppercase muted panel titles; thin --grid hairlines between feed rows; no shadows, gradients, animation or decoration. Watch the traps the browser check measures: a grid or flex display on rows overrides the hidden attribute unless you add [hidden] { display: none }; the bars' ::before labels must be absolutely positioned so they are not flex items; percentage widths of bar segments must not be squeezed (flex: none), and segments as blocks. (3) dashboard/tests/look.test.ts: a smoke test of the layout.

You write TypeScript for dashboard/, a Node project of its own inside a Python repository (package.json, tsconfig.json and vite.config.ts are in dashboard/; every command runs there). TypeScript strict, ESM imports with relative paths and no file extension ("./api"), no `any` (use `unknown` and narrow). 

Guardrail Frontend Isolation is checked on the syntax tree of every file in dashboard/src: no explicit any; data reaches the DOM only through textContent and setAttribute (no HTML-string properties); no console; the globals fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket, the timer functions, document, window and globalThis are named only in src/main.ts; src/format.ts and src/feed.ts import nothing; only relative imports.

Your own test file is smoke only: 1 to 5 vitest `test(...)` calls, comparing scalars and short values with `toBe`, never `toEqual` on fixture-sized arrays or objects. Import `test`/`expect` from "vitest" and every stub (fixtures, fake fetch, fake clock, synthetic events) from "./helpers"; declare no fetch or Fake* of your own and do not stub globals. A test writes no file and opens no connection. Completeness is judged by a probe built from the Contour examples, not by your test.

The acceptance builds the page and measures it in headless Chrome against the four fixtures (Style Page examples 1-8): every failed check prints one line "Style Page exN: ...".

Read docs/TASK_PHASE17.md FIRST (sections 2.3 and 3.2), then in contour.yaml group dashboard-ui the Function Wire Page: its examples 6, 7, 8 and 9 (the phase-17 layout) are the tests you write, one vitest `test` per example, named "Wire Page ex<N>: <short what>", in example order; you may add up to 12 more tests for rules of its "Phase 17 (layout)" paragraph. Examples 1-5 are already tested in tests/main.examples.test.ts and Style Page is measured in a browser by the orchestrator's probe: do not test either. Write ONLY dashboard/tests/look.examples.test.ts; do not write or modify dashboard/src/main.ts or dashboard/src/style.css -- the author of the criterion is not the author of the code. Read the code to learn how to call it, never to decide what it should return: the Contour decides.

You write TypeScript for dashboard/, a Node project of its own inside a Python repository (package.json, tsconfig.json and vite.config.ts are in dashboard/; every command runs there). TypeScript strict, ESM imports with relative paths and no file extension ("./api"), no `any` (use `unknown` and narrow). 

Import from "vitest", start from "../src/main" and every stub from "./helpers" (loadFixture, fixtureEvents, fixtureFetch, fakeFetch, fakeClock, flush); declare no fetch or Fake* of your own, do not stub globals (vi.spyOn on console is fine). Give every test a fresh <div id="app"> in document.body. No test.skip/only/todo. A test writes no file. The global `document` is happy-dom's.
